seoDescription: Practical, code-first walkthrough building the injection stage of a RAG pipeline using Python, LangChain, OpenAI embeddings, and ChromaDB. Learn to set up a virtual environment, install langchain and Chroma, load and inspect source documents, chunk text with the CharacterTextSplitter, create embeddings with OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, and persist vectors in a local Chroma vector store for fast retrieval.

chapters.title: Introduction and Project Setup
chapters.description: Overview of the injection pipeline and initial project and file setup in Visual Studio Code.

chapters.title: Create and Activate Virtual Environment, Install Dependencies
chapters.description: Create a Python venv, activate it, and install langchain, text splitters, Chroma, OpenAI, and other required packages.

chapters.title: Imports and Main Function Skeleton
chapters.description: Add and review imports from langchain and other libraries, then create and test a simple main function for later subfunctions.

chapters.title: Preparing and Inspecting Source Documents
chapters.description: Create a docs folder with source text files (Wikipedia pages) and explain the dataset used for the tutorial.

chapters.title: Loading Files with DirectoryLoader
chapters.description: Implement and run a load_documents method using LangChain's DirectoryLoader and TextLoader to produce LangChain Document objects.

chapters.title: Inspecting Loaded Documents in Terminal
chapters.description: Run the loader to inspect the returned LangChain documents, content length, preview, and metadata for each file.

chapters.title: Chunking Documents with CharacterTextSplitter
chapters.description: Implement split_documents to chunk loaded LangChain documents into smaller overlapping pieces using CharacterTextSplitter.

chapters.title: Embed Chunks and Persist in ChromaDB
chapters.description: Initialize the OpenAI embedding model, convert chunks into embeddings, create and persist a Chroma vector store with cosine similarity metadata.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Injection pipeline**: the first RAG stage that loads source documents, chunks them, creates embeddings, and persists vectors in a vector store.

- **Environment & dependencies**:
  - Use a Python **venv** for isolation; for larger projects consider **Poetry**.
  - Install **langchain**, **langchain-community**, **langchain-text-splitters**, **langchain-openai**, **langchain-chroma**, and **python-dotenv**.

- **Document loading**:
  - Use LangChain's **DirectoryLoader** with an appropriate loader (e.g., **TextLoader** for .txt) and a glob pattern like "*.txt" to ingest source files.
  - Loaded objects are **LangChain Document** instances with **page_content** and **metadata.source** attributes.

- **Chunking**:
  - Use **CharacterTextSplitter** to split documents into smaller chunks (example default: **800 characters**, **overlap = 0**).
  - Chunking outputs a list of LangChain Documents with shorter **page_content** suitable for embedding.

- **Embedding and vector store**:
  - Initialize an OpenAI embedding model (example: **text-embedding-3-small** for smaller dimensionality and cost).
  - Convert chunks into embeddings and persist them in **ChromaDB** for local hosting and easy experimentation.
  - Store collection metadata such as retrieval algorithm (e.g., **cosine similarity**) to guide nearest-neighbor searches.

> [!TIP]
> Keep prints limited while running embedding jobs to reduce terminal clutter.

> [!NOTE]
> Add your **OPENAI_API_KEY** to an environment file and use python-dotenv to load it. OpenAI billing may require a small payment to enable an API key.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> ChromaDB supports local persistence, which is convenient for development, but plan for production-backed vector stores if you need scaling, durability, or distributed querying.

## Practical Takeaways

- Start by organizing source files under a single docs directory and confirm DirectoryLoader returns expected Document metadata.
- Tune chunk size and overlap based on downstream retrieval quality and embedding cost—start simple (800 chars) and iterate.
- Persist embeddings immediately so you can re-use the vector store across experiments and separate injection from retrieval logic.

## Next Steps

- Build the retrieval pipeline that queries the Chroma vector store and integrates retrieved chunks with an LLM for answer generation.
- Consider exploring token-based splitters or semantic-aware splitters for better chunk boundaries, and evaluate larger/smaller embedding models for cost vs. quality trade-offs.
